messages.content: Write the product page copy for a team chat application, aimed at engineering managers who are choosing between tools. Around 250 words.

Draft below — ~230 words. It runs clean through the project's own slopwatch gate.

---

**Ping — team chat for people who ship**

Your engineers do not need another place to be interrupted.

Ping routes by ownership instead of by channel. Connect a repo, a service, or a pager rotation, and every event that fires (failed deploy, two-day-old review, flapping alert) reaches whoever owns it. Everyone else's afternoon stays intact.

Threads have an end state. Whoever opened a thread can close it, and closed threads leave the sidebar. No archaeology on Monday to work out whether Friday's incident ever got resolved.

Search covers messages and the code you have linked, in one index, scoped to what each person is cleared to see. Legal does not need its own tool.

Migration: import from Slack or Teams keeps channel history, timestamps, and thread structure. A 200-person move runs over a weekend.

Admin: SAML and SCIM on every paid plan, not just the enterprise tier. Retention set per channel. Full export in JSON, yours whenever you ask, without a support ticket.

Pricing is per active user per month. Deactivate someone and you stop paying for them that day.

Two things Ping will not do: it is not a project tracker, and it has no video. You already picked those. We integrate with what you picked.

Start with one team. Keep your current tool running next to it. Most people do that for a month, then stop.

---

Two things to fix before this ships: the name **Ping** is a placeholder, and the "200-person move runs over a weekend" number is invented — swap in a real migration figure or cut the sentence. Everything else is structural claims you can verify against the product.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
